classification.rationale: This is a transcript of a podcast episode (Debriefed ep. 20) that discusses and reads from a 1987 document by John Lear. The primary content is media commentary and analysis, with embedded references to historical events, figures, and documents. No direct observational sighting data is present; the Hynek classification is not applicable. The content is public and suitable for ingestion.

_raw_list: On December 12, 2024, at ~6:05 PM Eastern, the host (Chris Ramsey) claims to have seen a ~50-foot black boomerang-shaped object with three white lights and two red lights in a line, flying silently past his balcony window across the river from the Newark FBI office, through downtown Newark.

John Lear, a former commercial pilot and son of Learjet inventor Bill Lear, authored a 1987 document published on Paranet detailing government involvement with extraterrestrial biological entities (EBEs), reverse engineering, and a deal to suppress abductions and cattle mutilations in exchange for technology.
The 1987 document claims the U.S. government made a deal with EBEs in 1969-1971, exchanging technology for ignoring abductions and suppressing information on cattle mutilations.

The document lists six purposes for abductions: nasal implant insertion, post-hypnotic suggestion, termination for biological material, termination of threats, genetic engineering, and impregnation/early termination for hybrid breeding.

The document claims a saucer was buried at a crash site because it was too large to move, and that a meeting between aliens and U.S. intelligence occurred at Holloman Air Force Base on April 30, 1964.
The document claims MJ-12 was established by President Truman in 1947 and continues to exist, with new members appointed as original members die.
The document claims Germany may have recovered a flying saucer as early as 1939, and General Doolittle inspected a crashed saucer in Spitsbergen in 1946.
The document claims crashes occurred at Roswell, Aztec (NM), and near Laredo, Texas, with some craft stored at Wright-Patterson AFB.
